precepts.text: The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.
precepts.point: The Lord will bring Israel up out of the land of the north, North America.
precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God.” That is America going into space; America was the first there, and America invented the airplane that ascends “above the heights of the clouds.” “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north.” That is the Monroe Doctrine, now the Donroe Doctrine. The congregation is Mexico, Central and South America, Panama, Puerto Rico, Dominica, Jamaica, Trinidad and the Caribbean islands, where the twelve tribes of Israel are. America, the king of Babylon, the oppressor, sits upon the congregation and rules over us: fall in line, or what we did to Maduro we will do to you. And it is in the sides of the north, North America; that is why its treaty with Europe is called the North Atlantic Treaty.

Jeremiah shows where Israel is: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” The land of the north is North America. It is going to be said that the Lord brought the children of Israel out of this side of the world.

“and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” Israel is in North America and all through this hemisphere, and 2 Esdras speaks of the ten tribes coming to this side of the world.

So the one who sits on the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north is sitting on Israel. According to prophecy, America will be sitting on these congregations in the last days, during the fourth seal, and bad things are about to happen on this side of the world. But the Lord will bring his people up out of the land of the north.

precepts.text: It shall no more be said, the Lord liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“I have redeemed thee.” Jeremiah shows that this redemption will be greater than the first: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, he destroyed Ethiopia and he destroyed Seba, Somalia.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” The land of the north is North America. All the lands whither he had driven them are the Caribbean, Africa, and all the different lands we are scattered in.

“and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is Isaiah 43: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.” We are here in the west, the western hemisphere.

So the redemption promised to Jacob is not the one out of ancient Egypt. It is the deliverance out of the land of the north and every land of our captivity, and it will be so great that the Exodus will no longer be what men speak of.

precepts.text: No more Blessed be the Lord that brought Israel out of Egypt, but out of the land of the north; the greater exodus is still ahead.
precepts.point: The same deliverance will be told again: it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, but, The Lord liveth that brought them up from the land of the north, out of Babylon the Great where the people sit today.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt”: that is what Israel does every year at the Passover, giving honour to the things he did in Egypt and the way he delivered the people out of the hand of the oppressors.

But the telling of Egypt is not the last telling. “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

The greater exodus is still ahead. The people sit today in the land of the north, in Babylon the Great, and the Lord will bring them up from there and from all the lands where he drove them, back into the land he gave their fathers. Then what the fathers tell their sons will be that deliverance, and by it the sons will know how that he is the Lord.

precepts.text: Because your fathers have forsaken me and walked after other gods, and ye have done worse than your fathers, therefore will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, where I will not shew you favour.
precepts.point: The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up.

note.label: Numbers 6: The Law of the Nazarite and the Blessing of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The Lord lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.” All of that is a stipulation, a contract; it is not unconditional love with the Most High. Keep my commandments and live.

When the southern kingdom asked, “Wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? or what is our iniquity? or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?”, the answer was: “Because your fathers have forsaken me, saith the Lord, and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law; And ye have done worse than your fathers; for, behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart, that they may not hearken unto me.”

Bring it up to today: Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, every denomination walking after the imagination of its own evil heart. “Therefore will I cast you out of this land into a land that ye know not, neither ye nor your fathers; and there shall ye serve other gods day and night; where I will not shew you favour.” Cast out into a land we knew not, serving gods where the Lord shows no favor: that is why our people have no peace and no blessing.

The Most High has taken that blessing from us, and we have to work to get it back by repentance and enduring to the end. But it will happen again; the Lord is pulling his spirit back out on us, and the remnant is waking up.

precepts.text: The days come that it shall no more be said the Lord liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt, but the Lord liveth that brought the children of Israel from the land of the north, which is North America, and from all the lands whither he had driven them; if the people in the land now were not Israel, why are they still here in New York, Hollywood, and Miami.
precepts.point: Great deliverance he gives to his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The great deliverance and mercy shown to David's seed for evermore is spelled out in Jeremiah: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them”.

The land of the north is North America. He brings the children of Israel from there and from all the lands where he drove them, “and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

If the people in the land now were not Israel, why are they still here in New York, Hollywood, and Miami? The Most High put us here, and it is he who brings us back, the deliverance he gives to his king and his seed for evermore.

precepts.text: The days come when it shall no more be said the Most High liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt, but that brought them from the land of the north, which is North America.
precepts.point: David will speak of the glorious honor of His majesty and His terrible acts and declare His greatness. When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
“One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts.” When the kingdom comes we will have something new to talk about, no longer only the deliverance of the past: “it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.”

The land of the north is North America. That is the mighty act the next generation will declare.

precepts.text: I will send for many fishers, and after will I send for many hunters.
precepts.point: Peter and Andrew straightway left their nets. That was their living, and they left it without hesitation. Many in this truth have been in it for years and know little, because they were not willing to give up what they were building.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
Christ told Simon Peter and Andrew, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” Jeremiah wrote of this: “Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the Lord, and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks.”

The fishers come first; the hunters come after. Christ calling fishers to be fishers of men is the Lord sending for the many fishers. The hunters, who hunt them from every mountain and hill and out of the holes of the rocks, come afterward.

precepts.text: The Most High said, I will send for many fishers, and they shall fish them; a fisher does not stay in one spot, so he persecutes you in one city to send you to another to fish out those Israelites. This is chess, not checkers.
precepts.point: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the Lord, and they shall fish them”. A fisher does not stay in one spot. So the Most High persecutes you in one city to send you to another to fish out those Israelites. That is why “they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word”: the persecution was the Most High moving his fishers. This is chess, not checkers.

Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition. You might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

moments.label: 250 Years of Celebration; 400 Years of Sweat Equity!

points: So now think about this. Israel is going to say, why? Because leadership been saying there's going to be another Trayvon Martin, there's going to be another Mike Brown, there's going to be another Sandra Bland, there's going to be another, another, another. Our people say, why is all this evil happening to us? We just read some are from death to death, some are from sword to sword, some are from famine to famine. Why is all this evil happening to our people?

Or what is our iniquity? Our people have to get to the point of, how have we offended or transgressed against God? They're not asking that. They're asking why is this stuff happening. But they're not asking what is our transgression. Meaning they have not found out, realised or accepted that these things are happening to us because of what? Because of our sins.

This is what our people knew in the past and we're bringing to the forefront of our people's minds today. When you brothers is going out into the highways and hedges, whether you're giving out a flyer, teaching one on one, in passing, giving someone understanding, this is what they have to realise. These things are happening to us because of our sins. This is why we teach with such fervency, such urgency, because we know there's going to be another Trayvon. We know there's going to be another Nolan Wells.

So when our people like, oh, they're so loud — we know the type of wickedness our people are into, and we try to warn them. Listen, judgment is coming from God. Come out of that wickedness. Amend your ways. Change your ways. God's judgment is coming.

Then this is what you say when they finally come to their understanding: what is our sin? Because your fathers have forsaken me. So because our forefathers forsook the Lord. And have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law.

Wait, what does the Bible say? And ye have done worse than your fathers. So our forefathers transgressed the commandments of God, and now the children, which is us today, are like, what did we do that was so bad? The Lord said, you're actually worse than your forefathers. Damn, you're worse. That's what the Lord said.

For behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart. Of his what? Of his evil heart. No, his good and right heart? His evil heart. God says your heart is wicked as hell, and you do worse than your forefathers. The Lord made our forefathers walk in the wilderness for forty years. The Lord said, yo, y'all worse. Or, we're worse. I'll say that.

When we go into the scriptures, as we stand on those corners and prophesy, they going to say, wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? I thought y'all said we was his chosen people. What is our iniquity? What is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God? When we go to Zechariah 11, we show them: whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty. When we go into Isaiah, we show them we're going to be massly incarcerated, hidden in prison houses.

Then shalt thou say unto them, Because your fathers have forsaken me: your mother taught you birthdays. Your daddy taught you Christmas. And have walked after other gods: and your grandma taught you white Jesus. And have served them, and have worshipped them: and you serve them with that cross around your neck. And have forsaken me, and have not kept my law: you don't keep commandment one.

And ye have done worse than your fathers: our people have done worse than their parents. For behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart, that they may not hearken unto me. So we got to remember: Christ was not emotional. Christ ain't get caught up. He understood what was going on. It's all part of the program.

It shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt: that deliverance is still on the people's minds now. But the way they sat on our mentality, the world does not know the Bible is talking about us. That is how well they hid us; they manufactured a people and said these are the people the Bible speaks of. A total lie. You are the Jews; you are the Israelites.

But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north: something so spectacular, so magnificent, and so marvelous has to happen that it makes us stop talking about ancient Egypt, the Red Sea, and the ten plagues. That is going to be when he delivers us from here, from the land of the north: the same place where we are being oppressed.
